items.title: A.I. videos flooded the internet in the run-up to the election.
items.author: Ana Ionova
items.summary: The internet experienced a significant surge in AI-generated videos during the period leading up to the recent election. These synthetic media creations raised concerns regarding the spread of misinformation and the integrity of digital discourse.

brief.what: A proliferation of AI-generated videos appeared online throughout the election cycle. These digital assets utilized advanced technology to create synthetic content that reached a broad audience.
brief.who: Internet users and political observers are the primary actors witnessing the impact of these AI-driven media campaigns.
brief.context: The rise of generative artificial intelligence has made it increasingly simple to produce realistic but fabricated video content, complicating the information landscape for voters.
brief.why: The article suggests this trend occurred due to the accessibility of AI tools that allow for the rapid creation and dissemination of synthetic media.

earlier.title: A.I. Election Videos Are Flooding Brazil. Could They Sway the Vote?

items.title: CEO SUNDAY: Atomic Wings CEO shares his journey from Wall Street to the restaurant business
items.summary: Atomic Wings CEO Zak Omar discusses his transition from a Wall Street IT career to leading a growing restaurant franchise. He emphasizes the importance of customer service, team development, and reflective leadership practices.

brief.what: Atomic Wings CEO Zak Omar is expanding his restaurant chain to 40 locations by the end of the year, up from the current 35. Omar attributes his leadership style to a weekly habit of analyzing successes and failures to drive continuous improvement.
brief.who: Zak Omar is the CEO of Atomic Wings, a fast-casual restaurant chain specializing in chicken wings and tenders.
brief.context: Omar transitioned into the restaurant industry after a career in IT on Wall Street, following personal health challenges involving a leukemia diagnosis and his father's hospitalization.
brief.why: Omar believes that prioritizing the success of his team and franchisees is the primary driver of the company's growth, noting that the business is fundamentally about customer service rather than just food.
brief.next: The company plans to reach 40 locations by the end of the year.
